pages.title: What a verified chain tells you
pages.description: Integrity, external checkpoints and signer identity answer different questions.

sections.title: Three distinct questions
paragraphs: Digest links detect inconsistencies within the chain. A previously trusted external head is needed to detect tail removal or a completely recomputed history.
A signature identifies a signing key under a verification policy. It does not prove that a test passed, or independently establish when another party observed the head.

name: Nostoi
tagline: Records that should survive. Chains you can verify.
description: A Rust library, CLI and terminal interface for verifying, appending, streaming and browsing tamper-evident audit chains.

sections.title: Verify the history, locate the break
paragraphs: Nostoi reads its own nostoi-v1 JSON Lines and append-only SQLite stores, WeftMark ledgers, and Ephor audit stores. Verification identifies the first inconsistent record; a broken chain is never extended.
The portable core has no networking, CLI or Linux dependency. Native Python bindings and WebAssembly interfaces are available in the checkout.

sections.title: A chain is only part of the answer
paragraphs: Hash links detect changes within a chain. Detecting a removed tail or a completely recomputed history needs a previously trusted head retained outside it.

Remote checkpoints, multi-destination anchoring and signed attestations keep integrity, signer identity and external observation distinct. Signing keys belong with their operators, not in a public website Worker.

sections.title: Shared evidence infrastructure
paragraphs: Nostoi gives Frog, Sylvae and other RAGBAZ projects a common chain format, and verifies the ledgers those projects already keep. This website publishes project information; it does not claim to verify an uploaded chain or signature.
